loop.text: What Shannon showed was that predicting text and compressing it are, in effect, the same problem. It is tempting to conclude that a model which predicts well must understand what it reads, but a low loss is not tantamount to understanding. Xie's account of in-context learning is predicated on the model fitting its training data exactly, so whether prompting resembles Bayesian inference is contingent on assumptions that real models may not meet. Attention maps are suggestive, yet a map is not, in and of itself, an explanation. The theory-of-mind results should give us pause: accuracy collapses after small changes to the story. By the same token, people stumble on some of those changes too, so the burden of proof lies with whoever claims more. Piantadosi and Hill stop short of saying that models understand as we do, and for now the jury is still out.
